title: Sandbox concurrency and rumor provenance
summary: Keep scheduling and world time distinct. Current v1 implements serialized authority plus stale-head rejection; queue and transparent_fork remain unsupported. Proposed expedition calendars and truth assessments require migration.

claims.statement: The reproduced Robbins protocol puts destinations and group assembly in players’ hands, coordinated with the referee. Shared reports and maps connect expeditions without proving every character knows every private fact.

Alexander proposes real-day/campaign-day correspondence, then addresses journeys that outrun the calendar using character/location lockdowns. This is one design, not a universal West Marches requirement.
Rumor content, provenance and underlying truth differ. Rumors can be partial or mixed, and changing circumstances can make an earlier report outdated. Sharing can remain an explicit player choice.

rules: A stale solo action after a raid commit returns CONFLICT without queuing, rebasing or forking automatically.
Rumor assessments bind assessed_at_sequence and evaluated_world_time; never leak them as narrator hints or retrieval-ranking side channels.
Keep existing ClaimRecord.acquired_at plus sequence cutoff; backdating occurrence cannot backdate knowledge.
Party membership alone grants no member’s private claim. Sharing commits specify eligible observers and party disclosure.
Do not insert late expedition actions behind the committed ledger head; new scheduling semantics need a reviewed migration.

open_questions: Canonical Robbins URLs https://arsludi.lamemage.com/index.php/78/grand-experiments-west-marches/ and follow-ups returned403. The transcription is inspected evidence, not authenticated original retrieval; exclude its AI summary.
No retroactive expedition scheduler or authoritative rumor truth classifier is implemented in v1.
